Content:
Pure Marxist analysis is fundamentally about conflict as the engine of history. Class struggle is permanent, violent, and structural. The dictatorship of the proletariat is a necessary stage of repression — you NEED coercion because the bourgeoisie and their ideology don't disappear after the revolution, they persist as false consciousness that must be actively combated. The state is always an instrument of class domination, even the workers' state — it just dominates a different class. International revolution requires active intervention because capitalism is a global system that will crush isolated socialist states through economic and military pressure.

The ASOIAF convention takes this cynicism further: power corrupts regardless of ideology, revolutionary leaders become the next tyrants, the wheel keeps turning. This is the "dark realism" school where all political systems converge on exploitation because sentient beings are fundamentally self-interested.
